items.title: Retail theft increasingly 'sophisticated' and now work of organized crime, experts say
items.summary: Retail theft has evolved from individual shoplifting into a crime increasingly committed by organized criminal networks, according to Peel Regional Police.

items.title: Mississauga and Brampton Houses of Worship to See More Police on Oct. 7 Anniversary
items.summary: According to Insauga, Peel Regional Police say officers will be visible at Muslim and Jewish places of worship in Mississauga and Brampton on Tuesday, the anniversary of the Oct. 7, 2023 attack in Israel. Police said in a release that they are aware of planned demonstrations and want everyone in the community to be able to gather, worship and demonstrate safely and peacefully. Insauga reports the 2023 attack involved coordinated armed incursions from Gaza into southern Israel during the Jewish holiday of Simchat Torah, killing more than 1,000 people including 36 children, with more than 360 civilians killed at the Nova music festival and over 250 taken hostage. Israel's military operation in Gaza has continued since. Peel police asked anyone attending demonstrations or community gatherings to remain peaceful and let others worship without fear or intimidation. The force said a similar announcement came from Durham Regional Police, which increased patrols near Jewish places of worship during Yom Kippur after antisemitic threats were made. Peel police said it takes any hate-motivated threats or actions against community members seriously and will respond accordingly.

items.title: Ditch the personal insults in Mississauga mayoral race, majority of voters tells poll
items.summary: A strong majority of Mississauga residents says personal insults don’t belong in mayoral debates or anywhere else during the election campaign, a new poll shows. Conducted immediately following the contentious Oct. ” Additionally, the survey showed 14 per cent of respondents described the 2026 Mississauga mayoral campaign as mostly respectful. Mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie engaged in a number of heated exchanges during last Thursday’s debate, the second this election season featuring the four highest-profile candidates. The two main rivals have also traded assorted jabs and attacks on social media during the campaign. City councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla are also among the 14 candidates vying for the top elected position in Mississauga. While they’ve taken one another — and Parrish and Crombie — to task on various issues during the first handful of debates, the bulk of the most contentious exchanges has taken place between the current mayor and her predecessor. Voters will go to the polls on Oct. 26 — though many may consider advance voting, which began on Tuesday. Liaison Strategies, a national public opinion research firm, released the poll results on Tuesday. The pollster said it surveyed a random sample of 1,000 Mississauga residents from Oct. 2-4, using Interactive Voice Recording technology. Participants were reached through random digit dialing across both landline and cellphone networks.

items.title: Port Credit's Fall'N The Port Festival Brings Alpacas, Scarecrow Hunt and a Shot at Riding a 'Unicorn'
items.summary: According to Insauga, the Fall'N The Port festival takes over Brant Avenue in Port Credit later this month with farm animals, crafts and live entertainment for families. Insauga reports one of the event's biggest draws will be a petting area with alpacas, goats, rabbits and a donkey, alongside face painting and busking performers. Organizers are also hiding 30 scarecrows across participating Port Credit businesses for a neighbourhood-wide hunt, with maps available at the BIA tent. Families who find and identify all 30 scarecrows can enter a draw for a family prize pack. Insauga reports the grand prize gives one winner the chance to ride a unicorn, or at least a convincing stand-in for one.

items.title: Mississauga-Raised Marvel Star Simu Liu Marries Allison Hsu in France
items.summary: According to Insauga, Marvel star and Mississauga native Simu Liu married Allison Hsu in France over the weekend of Oct. 3. The couple, who have been dating since late 2022, got engaged in Paris in May 2025. Hsu works as vice president of digital marketing at Interscope Records. Liu, who came to Canada from Harbin, China at age five and grew up near Winston Churchill Boulevard attending Thorn Lodge Public School, got his start on the Canadian sitcom Kim's Convenience before his career took off with the 2021 Marvel film Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings. Insauga reports he's since appeared in the sci-fi spy series The Copenhagen Test and has a role in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, and was inducted into Mississauga's Legends Row Walk of Fame in 2024.

items.title: 60-Year-Old Charged After Tedjo Campaign Volunteer Disarmed Knife-Wielding Attacker in Mississauga
items.summary: According to CP24, Peel Regional Police have charged a 60-year-old man with assault with a weapon after he threatened a volunteer for mayoral candidate Alvin Tedjo with a knife while the volunteer was installing election signs near Truscott Drive and Southdown Road on Monday night. Police say the volunteer managed to disarm the suspect during the confrontation and sustained only minor injuries. The suspect, who police have not publicly identified, was released on an undertaking and is scheduled to appear in the Ontario Court of Justice at a later date. Tedjo addressed the incident in a statement Tuesday, saying the volunteer was confronted by a stranger and attacked while putting up campaign signs. He said he has spoken with the volunteer to offer support and has been in touch with Peel Police as they investigate. CP24 reports the Mississauga mayoral election is scheduled for Oct. 26.

items.title: Six-Year-Old Reported Missing From Whitby Turns Up Safe in Mississauga
items.summary: According to Insauga, Durham Regional Police say a six-year-old girl who went missing from the area of Dundas Street and Thickson Road in Whitby on Saturday has been found safe in Mississauga. Her disappearance prompted a wide search and a public appeal for help from media and the community. Police said the girl was located shortly after noon Monday with the help of tips from the public and media coverage, in the company of Blair Hamilton, a friend of her father's. Hamilton has not been charged, and police said the circumstances of her disappearance remain under investigation. Insauga reports police thanked everyone who helped in the search, calling it a positive and successful outcome.
